clue.text: Testimonials on the subject of barriers around monarch

parts.note: RE is Latin-derived shorthand meaning concerning or about

indicators.note: around says the fences surround the monarch's letters

parts.note: fences are barriers around a field
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the crossword monarch

explanation.surface: Character references are being written about the barricades put up around the sovereign.
explanation.definitionFit: Testimonials and these are both written statements vouching for someone's character, as for a job application.

clue.text: Remove symbol of royalty from record, with name below line

indicators.note: in a down entry, below means the name's letter comes after the line

parts.note: a disc is a gramophone record
a row is a line of things side by side

explanation.surface: Instructions for stripping a crown emblem from a vinyl record and writing a name under a rule.
explanation.definitionFit: To discrown is to depose a monarch, literally taking away the crown, the chief royal emblem.

clue.text: For example, spots rising fare unpalatable to consumers

indicators.note: in a down clue, rising means both pieces are read from the bottom up

parts.note: EG abbreviates exempli gratia, for example
dots are spots

explanation.surface: A complaint that a dish, with spots coming up on it, is food diners cannot stomach.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rising' turns EGDOTS round, which is why the clue's first piece ends up last.
explanation.definitionFit: Stodge is heavy, starchy food that sits leaden in the stomach, hard going for anyone eating it.

clue.text: Dump all you possess, ultimately — that's a positive sign

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter of each of the four words before it

explanation.surface: Decluttering advice: get rid of all your belongings, and that's a good thing.
explanation.definitionFit: The plus symbol is the mathematical mark for a positive quantity or addition.

clue.text: Generous letters he has delivered outside

indicators.note: outside says the freed letters go round the others

parts.note: delivered in the sense of rescued or set free, freed
the word he is made of the letters H and E, read as H AND E

explanation.surface: A postman is praised for being generous with the mail he has brought to someone outside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'letters he has' reads as the letters in HE, spelt out as H AND E, which FREED wraps round.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone open-handed and liberal in giving is said to be free-handed, giving without stinting.

clue.text: Kind of alcohol available in labs, in theory

indicators.note: available in says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A particular kind of spirit is said to be obtainable in laboratories, at least on paper.
explanation.definitionFit: Absinthe is a strong green anise-flavoured spirit, a specific type of liquor.

clue.text: Incite masked man in theatre, losing head

indicators.note: losing head says the first letter of the surgeon is dropped

parts.note: a surgeon wears a mask in the operating theatre

explanation.surface: Stirring up a masked figure on stage, who then loses his head.
explanation.walkthrough: 'theatre' suggests a stage; here it is a hospital operating theatre.
explanation.definitionFit: To urge someone on is to encourage or spur them into action, the phrasal verb for incite.

clue.text: Biological liquid container kept in pharmacy store

indicators.note: kept in says the answer is a run of letters held inside the following words

explanation.surface: A container for some bodily fluid is stored at the chemist's.
explanation.definitionFit: A cyst is a membranous sac in the body holding fluid, so a biological vessel for liquid.

clue.text: Bizarre replies to letter writer

indicators.note: bizarre means weird or twisted, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Odd responses addressed to a correspondent.
explanation.walkthrough: The across answers each hide a weapon: here PISTOL sits inside.
explanation.definitionFit: An epistoler is a writer of epistles, which are formal letters.

clue.text: British military force that's not all there

parts.note: an army is a military force

explanation.surface: A remark that a British fighting force has lost its wits.
explanation.walkthrough: ARM, a weapon, is hidden inside, as the theme demands.
explanation.definitionFit: Barmy is British slang for crazy, and not all there is the idiom for being mentally unsound.

clue.text: US codes broken — they no longer work in Europe

definitions.text: they no longer work in Europe

indicators.note: broken signals that the letters are smashed and reassembled

explanation.surface: American ciphers have been cracked, and some no longer function on the Continent.
explanation.walkthrough: The escudo was Portugal's currency until the euro replaced it; SCUD, a missile, is hidden.
explanation.definitionFit: The escudos were Portuguese coins and notes, withdrawn when the euro arrived, so no longer valid tender.

clue.text: Met nine or ten men I somehow distinguished

indicators.note: somehow says the letters arrive by some unspecified rearrangement

explanation.surface: Meeting a group of nine or ten men who somehow stood out.
explanation.walkthrough: Both 'Met nine' and 'ten men I' are anagrams of the answer, and 'somehow' serves either; MINE, a weapon, is hidden.
explanation.definitionFit: Eminent describes a person who is famous and respected in their field, standing out from others.

clue.text: Gradually reduce fear, with soldier ignoring the odds

indicators.note: ignoring the odds means only the even-numbered letters of each word are kept

explanation.surface: Advice to wear down fear, along with a soldier who disregards the betting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'odds' suggests betting; here it means the odd-numbered letters. ROD, slang for a gun, is hidden.
explanation.definitionFit: To erode is to wear away little by little, as water does to rock.

clue.text: Restrained Conservative went with expedition

parts.note: to go with expedition is to move with speed, which is to hurry

explanation.surface: A Tory who joined an exploring party has been reined in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'expedition' suggests a journey of exploration; here it means speed. STEN, a gun, is hidden.
explanation.definitionFit: Chastened means subdued or restrained, typically after being corrected or punished.

clue.text: Coming down pass, have a little drink and celebrate

parts.note: a col is a mountain pass
to lap is to drink by small tongue-flicks, like a cat
to sing can be to celebrate, as in singing someone's praises

explanation.surface: A party of climbers descending a mountain pass, stopping for a drink and a song.
explanation.definitionFit: Collapsing means falling down or caving in, so it is a way of coming down.

clue.text: Warning as gardening's gone wrong

indicators.note: gone wrong signals the letters are disordered

parts.note: the possessive here supplies its S as a letter for the shuffle

explanation.surface: An alert issued because the gardening has failed badly.
explanation.definitionFit: A danger sign is a notice or indication that alerts people to a hazard.

clue.text: Something offensive hidden in crosswords, say — and other across answers

definitions.text: Something offensive hidden in crosswords, say — and other across answers

parts.words: Something offensive hidden in crosswords, say — and other across answers
parts.note: the word sword lies inside crosswords, and every other across entry also conceals an arm

explanation.surface: Puzzles are said to contain something rude or offensive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'offensive' suggests rude; it means used for attack. SWORD hides in 'crosswords', and the other across entries hide PISTOL, ARM, SCUD, MINE, ROD, STEN, PIKE, UZI, GUN, EPEE, GAT and ARROW.
explanation.definitionFit: A concealed weapon is an arm carried out of sight, which is what each hidden word is.

clue.text: Performs, engaging in sometimes exaggerated accounts?

indicators.note: in says the charming word sits within the expenses

parts.note: exes is informal for expenses, claims sometimes padded
engaging means charming or appealing, cute

explanation.surface: A performer suspected of padding the figures in some tall stories.
explanation.definitionFit: To execute a task, dance or manoeuvre is to carry it out or perform it.

clue.text: No square meals in this restaurant?

definitions.text: No square meals in this restaurant?

parts.words: No square meals in this restaurant?
parts.note: a square meal is a hearty one, but here square is literal: the food served here is round

explanation.surface: A complaint about an eatery that offers no proper filling food.
explanation.definitionFit: A pizzeria is an Italian-style eatery serving flat round pies baked in an oven.

clue.text: Before a doctor returned, put alcohol in new ointment

indicators.note: Before says the spiking and the new letter come ahead of the rest

parts.note: to spike a drink is to secretly add alcohol to it

indicators.note: returned means the doctor's letters are turned back

explanation.surface: A doctor comes back, and someone laces a new salve with drink.
explanation.walkthrough: PIKE, a long spear, is the hidden weapon.
explanation.definitionFit: Spikenard is an aromatic balm from a Himalayan plant, used in ancient times as an ointment.

clue.text: Lives on old bank, on which pressure is constant

parts.note: lives here means exists, is
a bar is a sandbank across a river mouth

explanation.surface: Someone lives on an old riverbank under steady stress.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry 'on' stacks each piece over the next.
explanation.definitionFit: On a weather map, the line joining points of equal atmospheric pressure has the same reading all along.

clue.text: Girl's name, as usual, initially written in wrong size

indicators.note: written in says the first letter goes inside the jumbled size
wrong means the letters of size are put out of order
initially takes just the opening letter of the word before it

explanation.surface: A girl's name, written out as usual but in the wrong dress size.
explanation.walkthrough: The jumble SZIE takes U inside; UZI, the submachine gun, is hidden.
explanation.definitionFit: Suzie is a familiar form of Susan, a female first name.

clue.text: Audibly spelt out copper's parting statement

indicators.note: audibly spelt out means the two letters are said as their letter names

parts.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper

explanation.surface: A police officer's farewell, said out loud.
explanation.walkthrough: 'copper' suggests a police officer; here it is the metal, whose symbol is Cu.
explanation.definitionFit: This phrase is a casual farewell, said when leaving someone.

clue.text: Holding back game in Japan, avoids leaders there

indicators.note: Holding says the avoiding word contains the reversed game

parts.note: to shun is to avoid

indicators.note: back means the game's name is reversed

parts.note: go is a board game played with stones, popular in Japan

explanation.surface: Someone in Japan holds back from a game and keeps away from those in charge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'there' refers back to Japan. GUN is hidden.
explanation.definitionFit: Shoguns were the hereditary military rulers of feudal Japan.

clue.text: Animal found in loch as well as ocean

indicators.note: as well as joins the two pieces, the ocean coming first

parts.note: sea is a synonym of ocean
L is the abbreviation for lake or loch

explanation.surface: A creature to be found in a Scottish lake as well as at sea.
explanation.definitionFit: A seal is a flippered marine mammal.

clue.text: Drink with vegetables, we hear, in some North American homes

indicators.note: we hear signals that the words are said aloud to give a different spelling

parts.note: tea is a drink and peas are vegetables

explanation.surface: Tea served with vegetables in some American households.
explanation.walkthrough: EPEE, a fencing sword, is the hidden weapon.
explanation.definitionFit: Tepees are conical tents of the Plains peoples, so some native dwellings of the continent.

clue.text: Attempt to retain old prayer in Church of England?

indicators.note: to retain says the attempt holds the old letter inside

parts.note: a try is an attempt

explanation.surface: Trying to keep an ancient prayer in the Anglican church.
explanation.walkthrough: It inverts the old jibe that the Church of England is the Conservative Party at prayer.
explanation.definitionFit: The joke turns round a famous quip linking the Anglican church and the Conservative Party, here as a definition by example.

clue.text: Marble article placed in front of entrance

indicators.note: placed in front of puts the article before the entrance

parts.note: a is the indefinite article
a gate is an entrance

explanation.surface: A marble ornament stands before an entrance.
explanation.walkthrough: GAT, slang for a gun, is hidden.
explanation.definitionFit: An agate is a banded stone, and a playing marble made of or resembling it.

clue.text: Contracting, hurried back with work for crew

indicators.note: back means the hurrying word is reversed

parts.note: ran means hurried
rowing is what a boat's crew does

explanation.surface: A crew shrinking after a hurried return to work.
explanation.definitionFit: Narrowing means getting tighter or smaller, which is what contracting is.
